A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Revela and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. The material supports reliable comparison across the versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval experiments on CoIR, BRIGHT, and BEIR, together with ablations, generalization experiments, and LM capability evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains original retrieval experiments and appendix analyses, including revised BRIGHT results.

M1.justification: The joint retriever–LM objective, similarity-weighted in-batch attention, and optional V-normalization remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix B.5. The added attention explanation clarifies existing computations.

E1.justification: Both versions use Wikipedia, code-related corpora, and Fineweb-edu, and evaluate the same CoIR, BRIGHT, BEIR, and seven LM capability tasks. No represented domain or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the corresponding retrieval and controlled Contriever comparisons. The removed 8B Revela results concern a proposed-model configuration, while the REPLUG reference-LM clarification does not establish a changed comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported Wikipedia chunk ordering from round-robin across documents to consecutive chunks within each document before batching. It also removes the 8B BRIGHT configuration. These are localized setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish whether the ordering change reflects rerunning experiments or correcting the description.

E4.justification: Evidence in the retained LM-size sensitivity analysis changes slightly: v2 Table 12 becomes v3 Table 13, with one ClimateFEVER value revised and two TREC-COVID values exchanged. The analysis questions and other ablation, generalization, and LM-preservation studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: BRIGHT results are substantially revised in v2 Table 7 versus v3 Table 8: Revela 3B changes from 16.9 to 20.1 mean nDCG@10, E5-PT from 11.4 to 13.1, and REPLUG 3B from 9.9 to 12.2. Revela 3B now ranks above the unchanged 17.9 E5-Mistral and OpenAI/Voyage scores, and the 8B results disappear. Three BEIR LM-size ablation cells also change. These are reported result revisions without established same-setting comparability. V3 additionally claims a 3.1-point Revela 0.5B–E5-PT gap, although Table 8 gives 15.2 minus 13.1, or 2.1.

T1.justification: The attention and V-normalization equations, REPLUG KL objective, and linear-versus-quadratic complexity argument are retained. Matrix notation and Appendix C.7's Big-O presentation are refined without a substantive new derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction strengthen the BRIGHT claim from matching larger supervised models and proprietary APIs to surpassing them, with the results discussion now emphasizing Revela 3B instead of 8B. The central method, CoIR, efficiency, and scalability contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 adds an explicit explanation distinguishing sequence-only information from information carried through the in-batch stream. Section 5 adds the expectation that larger LMs preserve competitive general-domain performance while improving specialized retrieval. Other interpretations and future directions largely remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 explicitly identifies REPLUG's frozen LLaMA-3.2-1B reference LM, and Appendix B.4 adds an API access table. The BRIGHT caption newly attributes selected baseline scores to the benchmark paper. The new Cohere URL names a light variant despite the row's non-light model name, leaving an identification mismatch.

R1.justification: Sakaguchi et al. (2020) is newly cited for the already-used WinoGrande benchmark. Neelakantan et al. (2022), Cohere (2023), and Voyage AI (2024) references are removed as API information shifts to a URL table. Related-work positioning remains unchanged; CoIR's publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized prose revisions, adds the attention footnote, rewrites the efficiency explanation, standardizes metric and appendix references, and expands acknowledgments. The header changes to ICLR 2026 publication status, while the overall section structure remains.

P2.justification: V3 adds API URL Table 6 and revises the BRIGHT panel of Figure 3, including reordered bars, changed axis ticks, removal of 8B, and display of the previously tabulated 1B configuration. The BRIGHT table loses its 8B column; other changes mainly involve captions, spacing, and reflow.

improvement.justification: V3 improves attention explanations, implementation documentation, and benchmark attribution. However, revised BRIGHT scores accompany changed batching documentation without establishing experimental comparability, and Section 4.2 introduces an overstated gain: 3.1 points where Table 8 supports 2.1. The documentation benefits and weaker internal consistency leave the overall quality direction uncertain; higher reported scores alone do not resolve that tradeoff.
